findings.title: enableSqlExpressions is dead logic that always returns false
findings.body: `enableSqlExpressions` computes `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)` and then returns false on both branches, so the feature-flag read has no effect and the function is a constant `false`. While the intent (hard-disabling SQL expressions) is achieved, the code is misleading: a reader/linter can't tell whether the flag is honoured, and a future edit to one branch could silently re-enable the vulnerable path. Replace with an explicit `return false` plus a comment referencing CVE-2024-9264, or remove the helper and return the error directly.

findings.title: Error message 'sqlExpressions is not implemented' is misleading
findings.body: Users enabling the still-present `sqlExpressions` feature toggle will get 'sqlExpressions is not implemented', which suggests a missing feature rather than a deliberately disabled one. Since the toggle remains documented, the message should state that SQL expressions are currently disabled, so operators don't file bugs or assume a build problem.

findings.title: Legacy (non-reader) SQL expression path is not blocked, only stubbed
findings.body: `UnmarshalSQLCommand`/`NewSQLCommand` still accept SQL expression nodes; the feature-flag gate was only added in `reader.go` (ReadQuery). On the legacy query path, `sql.TablesList` now fails inside `NewSQLCommand`, returning a generic 'error reading SQL command' BadRequest, and `Execute` would return an opaque 'not implemented' as a query error. This makes the disable behaviour inconsistent and the failure mode confusing; the legacy path should explicitly reject SQL expressions with the same clear message.

findings.title: No test asserting SQL expressions are disabled
findings.body: This PR disables a security-sensitive feature purely by stubbing out the DB implementation and adding an always-false flag check, but no test asserts that a QueryTypeSQL query is rejected. Without such a test, a future refactor (e.g. reintroducing an engine or 'fixing' enableSqlExpressions) can silently re-enable the RCE/LFI path. Add a unit test for ReadQuery with QueryTypeSQL expecting an error.
